summary: Customer requests staged soft-offramp for dynamic batching + quantization + prefix cache after elevated 5xx and generation-quality drift
description: Issue summary: BrightDocs started a tenant-level optimizer experiment (dynamic batching + aggressive 4-bit quantization + prefix KV caching) yesterday 04:30 UTC. Since rollout, they report rising 5xx errors (rate ~2.3% of requests) and a measurable generation-quality regression on a tracked prompt set (BLEU/Rouge-like metric drop ~6%). Impact: production traffic affected for BrightDocs across us-east region; user-facing latencies increased and some long-running streams aborted. Environment: prod (us-east), tenant-scoped optimizer flags applied via console, model pinned to rwkd-13b-quant variant.
timeline:
2026-03-10 04:30 UTC - BrightDocs enabled tenant optimizer profile.
2026-03-10 05:10 UTC - First error spike observed on SLO dashboard (5xx increase).
2026-03-10 06:00 UTC - Customer message to support; included example request/response pairs.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Support engaged SRE; started triage.
2026-03-11 11:40 UTC - Observed correlation between high batch sizes, KV eviction events, and generator anomalies.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant toggles optimizer profile: dynamic_batching=on, kv_prefetch=on, quant_profile=aggressive-4bit.
2) Send steady stream of conversational requests with long histories.
3) Observe increase in tail latency and occasional 5xx from serving-runtime; verify outputs differ from baseline (pre-experiment) on known evaluation prompts.
logs_and_artifacts: Customer provided sample requests and a subset of failing streams. Support uploaded runtime logs to s3://redwood-support/brightdocs/SUP-853999/logs.tar.gz. Traces: trace IDs included in ticket thread. Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.io/d/serving/slo?tenant=brightdocs (private).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: combination of large dynamic batch windows with aggressive quantized kernels causes intermittent KV cache thrashing, leading to stale or misaligned KV lookups and occasional invalid memory access paths in the quantized model, triggering 5xx and quality drift. Evidence: 1) Periods of high batching coincide with KV eviction events in logs. 2) 5xx stack traces point to quantized kernel fallback paths and OOM-like transient errors. 3) Re-running sampled requests against non-quantized model variant produced expected outputs. Tests run in staging reproduced degraded outputs when both dynamic batching and kv_prefetch were enabled at high batch sizes.
Hypotheses prioritized: (A) reduce batching window to avoid large mixed-batch composition; (B) disable kv_prefetch tenant-side to remove eviction cycle; (C) temporarily switch to conservative quant profile (8-bit) for affected tenant.
proposed_action_plan:
1) Execute staged soft-offramp (non-disruptive): a) Configure tenant policy to cap batch size and reduce batching timeout by 50% (apply at 00:01 UTC). b) Monitor SLOs for 30 minutes. c) If 5xx/quality metrics remain, next step disable kv_prefetch for tenant (soft-offramp step 2). d) If still unresolved, switch tenant quant_profile to conservative-8bit and route traffic to compatible variant (step 3).
2) Use traffic-slow-drain and gradual demotion: divert 10% of traffic to fallback variant for 10 minutes, then 50%, then full.
3) Preserve traces and create snapshots of current optimizer flags before every change.
4) Coordinate changes in #support and #sre Slack; require approval from BrightDocs SRE lead before each stage.
5) Post-mortem: collect prompt set evaluation and model outputs pre/post change for regression analysis.
comments: 2026-03-11 09:12 - BrightDocs-SRE (Elena Morris): We're seeing ~2.2% of streams abort mid-response. We've attached examples and flagged the tenant optimizer change. Customer requests minimal disruption and a gradual rollback plan.

2026-03-11 11:45 - Jonah Rivera (Support): Triage started. Initial correlation suggests batching + kv_eviction. Proposing a staged soft-offramp that throttles batch growth before disabling kv_prefetch. Will coordinate a test window.

2026-03-11 13:02 - SRE (Marco Li): Ran reproducer in staging. When dynamic_batching window > 120ms and kv_prefetch=true on quant-4bit kernels, we saw sporadic kernel-fallback and higher error rates. Recommending stepwise demotion: cap batch size -> disable kv_prefetch -> revert quant profile.
2026-03-12 08:20 - BrightDocs-Eng (Priya Desai): We prefer the soft-offramp approach; please avoid full revert unless necessary. We can accept 10% diverted traffic initially for validation.
2026-03-13 02:00 - Jonah Rivera (Support): Implemented step 1a at 01:50 UTC (batch cap and reduced timeout). Monitoring dashboards; awaiting 30 minute window.
resolution_notes: (pending) Step 1a applied and under watch. No final resolution yet; plan documented and coordinated with BrightDocs. If steps 1-2 don't reduce 5xx and quality regressions within the next 6 hours, we will escalate to automatic rollback to conservative-8bit quant profile with staged traffic demotion. Create post-incident runbook entry and add test cases to optimizer regression suite.
follow_up_tasks: Create automated soft-offramp runbook in Confluence
Add regression test for combined dynamic batching + kv_prefetch + quantized kernels
Monitor tenant for 48 hours after full recovery
Schedule post-mortem meeting with BrightDocs and SRE
customer_communication: Initial acknowledgement sent 2026-03-11 09:20 UTC. We informed BrightDocs of staged approach and requested permission for 10% traffic diversion during validation windows. Will provide hourly updates until resolved.
